question.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform a Given Entry to a Desired Value
question.problem:
Given 
$A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 & 4 \\ -9 & 1 & -5 \\ 8 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}]$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{32}=0?$
question.worked_solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 & 4 \\ -9 & 1 & -5 \\ 8 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 & 4 \\ -9 & 1 & -5 \\ -4 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}.
$$

The complements are obtained by removing the specified set from its universal set: q-86587 gives {a,c}; q-102246 gives {n}; q-81203 gives the odd integers 1 through 9; q-105179 gives {2,6,10,14,18}; q-81205 gives the even integers that are not multiples of four; q-105188 gives letters k through z. q-73145: the leading entries sum to 1-3=-2. q-73148: they sum to -7+5+3=1. q-72491: A has leading columns 1,3,4,3 and C has 1,2,2,3, so both fail echelon form; B satisfies it. q-129213: A and B satisfy echelon form, while C has a zero row above nonzero rows. q-72575: under the standard definition, echelon form applies to the entire augmented matrix. A has leading columns 1,2,4,4 and B has 3,2,1, so both fail; C has 1,2,5 and satisfies it. MA explicitly applies a coefficient-matrix-only convention and consequently states B only. Its answer is preserved separately, but its definition and classification of A conflict with standard augmented-matrix echelon form. q-129232: A and C repeat leading columns, and B has a zero row above nonzero rows; all three fail. q-42008: zeroing a21 and a43 produces leading columns 1,2,3,4.
